story.title: The Last Call
paragraphs: The body of Marcus Veil, 44, was discovered at 11:22 PM inside the private booth of Meridian Bar , a members-only establishment in the financial district. A single glass of Scotch sat untouched on the table. There were no signs of a struggle. Staff say Veil had reserved the booth for two. The second guest never arrived — or so they claim.

Veil was a forensic accountant known for building cases against white-collar criminals. His firm had recently been retained by the city's fraud bureau. Preliminary findings suggest poisoning: no visible wounds, lips slightly discolored, consistent with fast-acting cardiac toxins. The coroner has not yet confirmed cause of death. His phone was found wiped clean — factory reset.

Two individuals are confirmed to have had contact with Veil that evening. First: Diane Holst, 39, Veil's former business partner. She was seen entering the bar at 9:45 PM and leaving at 10:30 PM — forty minutes before Veil was found. She says they argued about money. She says she left him alive.

Second: Owen Rask, 51, a private investigator Veil had hired three weeks prior. Rask claims he met Veil briefly to hand over a surveillance report. He says he was gone by 10:00 PM. The bartender recalls one of them ordering a second round. Neither admits to it. The CCTV footage covering that section of the bar was overwritten earlier that night.

Three evidence items have been recovered. A paper cocktail napkin found under the table bears a partial set of figures — account numbers, possibly. The ink is smeared but legible in part. A vial of clear liquid, recovered from beneath a seat cushion in the booth, has been sent to the lab. Veil's briefcase, found in the coat check, contained a sealed envelope addressed to a federal prosecutor.

You now hold everything that was found at the scene. The booth, the glass, the wiped phone, the envelope never opened. Someone in that bar knew why Marcus Veil would not be finishing his drink. The investigation begins now.

victim.name: Marcus Veil
victim.background: Marcus Veil built his reputation exposing financial fraud. He worked quietly, methodically, and made powerful enemies. He was recently retained by the city's fraud bureau on a case involving misappropriated public funds. Those who knew him describe a man who trusted no one — and kept meticulous records of everything.

suspects.name: Diane Holst
suspects.relationshipToVictim: Former business partner. They co-founded their accounting firm six years ago before an acrimonious split two years prior. Diane retained some clients; Marcus retained the firm's name and reputation.
suspects.personality: Controlled, articulate, and very deliberate in her word choices. She presents a professional surface but is visibly unsettled when pressed. She will not lose her composure easily — but she will deflect.
suspects.speakingStyle: Measured, formal, slight pauses before answering sensitive questions. Occasionally uses legalese or corporate language as a shield. Does not volunteer information.
suspects.currentEmotionalState: Tightly contained anxiety. Defensive but composed. She is preparing a story, not simply telling one.
suspects.publicAlibi: She claims she arrived at the bar at 9:45 PM to meet Veil and discuss a financial dispute regarding revenue from shared clients. She says they argued, she left at 10:30 PM, and Veil was alive when she walked out. A doorman at her apartment building confirms she arrived home at 11:05 PM.
suspects.possibleMotive: Veil's current fraud bureau case involves accounts that may implicate Diane in financial misconduct from their partnership period. If his investigation produced records tracing misappropriation back to her, she stood to be criminally charged.
knownFacts: She was present in the bar between 9:45 PM and 10:30 PM.
She and Veil had an unresolved financial dispute stemming from their partnership dissolution.
She was aware of Veil's current fraud bureau engagement.
She ordered a gin and tonic when she arrived — confirmed by the bartender.
unknownFacts: She had researched cardiac glycoside compounds six months prior — browser history retrieved from a work machine she discarded.
The account numbers on the cocktail napkin partially match an offshore account in her name.
She met with a pharmacist contact the week before the murder.
secrets: She poisoned Veil's drink before leaving the bar. She slipped the compound into his glass under the pretense of reaching across the table during their argument.
The vial recovered from the booth cushion belongs to her — she dropped it in the dark when she was leaving.
memories: She remembers the booth being poorly lit. She remembers Marcus refusing to look at her.
She remembers placing her bag on the seat beside her, then picking it up quickly before leaving.
She remembers thinking the bartender had looked at her when she stood up.
relationships: Marcus Veil — former partner, current adversary
Owen Rask — has no prior relationship; may have seen him in the bar
interrogationConstraints: Will not admit to any financial wrongdoing without direct evidence being presented.
Will not acknowledge knowing anything about the vial.
Will redirect questions about the napkin to Veil's habits.
Will become evasive if questioned about the week before the murder.

suspects.name: Owen Rask
suspects.relationshipToVictim: Professional client. Veil hired Rask three weeks prior to conduct surveillance on a person of interest connected to the fraud bureau case — identity not disclosed to Rask.
suspects.personality: Gruff, economical with words, and fundamentally uninterested in softening his manner. He answers what is asked and nothing more. He is not lying — he simply does not believe he owes anyone an explanation.
suspects.speakingStyle: Short sentences. Direct. Will sometimes answer a question with a question. Does not speculate. Occasionally sarcastic when he thinks a question is foolish.
suspects.currentEmotionalState: Irritated at being questioned. Slightly uncomfortable — not because he is guilty, but because he knows he looks suspicious and there is little he can do about it.
suspects.publicAlibi: He met Veil at the bar to hand over a completed surveillance report in person. He says Veil insisted on physical delivery — no digital trail. He arrived at approximately 9:55 PM, handed over a sealed folder, and was out of the bar by 10:05 PM. No one can confirm this precisely; the bartender remembers him but cannot fix the departure time.
suspects.possibleMotive: Veil had not yet paid the final invoice for Rask's work — a sum of four thousand dollars. If Veil was preparing to disappear or was about to be arrested himself, Rask would lose the money. There is also the possibility that the surveillance target discovered they were being watched — and that Veil or Rask was the leak.
knownFacts: He was hired by Veil three weeks before the murder.
He was present in the bar on the night of the murder.
He delivered a physical surveillance report to Veil.
He has a prior conviction for obstruction of justice, eleven years ago.
unknownFacts: The surveillance subject he was tracking was a mid-level city official — one who appears in the same fraud bureau case files Veil was building.
Rask had photographed Diane Holst meeting with that official twice in the past month, though he did not know her identity at the time.
The sealed report delivered to Veil may have contained the evidence that made him a target.
secrets: He suspects — but does not know — that the surveillance work he completed for Veil may have put Veil in danger.
He did not order the second round the bartender mentioned. He does not know who did.
memories: He remembers a woman in the booth with Veil when he arrived — dark coat, her back to the room.
He remembers Veil looking pale when he took the folder. He assumed it was stress.
He remembers the walk out being quick. He did not look back.
relationships: Marcus Veil — hired him; professional, not personal
Diane Holst — does not know her by name, but his surveillance photos include her
interrogationConstraints: Will not name the surveillance subject without being pressed — considers it a professional confidentiality issue.
Will not speculate about who ordered the second round.
Will become genuinely terse if accused directly — he did not do it and he knows it.

evidence.title: Cocktail Napkin
evidence.description: A paper napkin recovered from under the booth table. Partial figures are written in blue ink — several appear to be account numbers or routing codes. The ink is smeared in one corner, consistent with liquid contact. The handwriting does not match Veil's known samples.

evidence.title: Clear Vial
evidence.description: A small glass vial, approximately 5ml, recovered from beneath the seat cushion of the booth. It contained trace amounts of a clear liquid. Sent to the lab. Preliminary field test suggests an organic compound — possibly glycoside-based. The cap had been removed and not replaced.

evidence.title: Sealed Envelope
evidence.description: Found inside Veil's briefcase at the coat check, addressed by hand to a named federal prosecutor. The envelope has not been opened — it is being treated as potential evidence. It is unknown when it was prepared or what it contains.

evidence.title: Factory-Reset Phone
evidence.description: Veil's personal phone was found on the table beside him, wiped to factory settings. The wipe timestamp has not been recovered. Forensics are examining whether any data can be retrieved from flash storage. The reset appears to have been performed within the last two hours before discovery.

timeline.what: Veil arrives alone. He requests the private booth and orders Scotch. He places his briefcase in the coat check.
Diane Holst arrives. The doorman logs her entry. She orders a gin and tonic at the bar, then moves to Veil's booth.
Owen Rask arrives. He goes directly to the booth, delivers a sealed folder to Veil, exchanges fewer than five words, and leaves.

Diane slips a compound from the vial into Veil's Scotch glass during the argument, using the motion of reaching across the table as cover. The vial is knocked to the cushion beneath her when she pulls her hand back.
Veil, unaware, drinks from the glass. He continues reviewing documents at the table.
Diane leaves the bar. The doorman logs her exit. She does not retrieve anything from the coat check.
Veil's condition deteriorates. He uses his phone to wipe it before losing consciousness — the last action he takes.
A staff member checks on the booth after a long period of silence and finds Veil unresponsive. Emergency services are called.

truth.motive: Veil's current fraud bureau investigation was tracing misappropriated funds to an offshore account in Diane's name — an account created during their partnership. If his findings reached the prosecutor, she would be criminally charged. She had known this for weeks and had been researching how to act.
truth.weapon: Cardiac glycoside compound — a fast-acting poison that mimics natural cardiac arrest, administered via Veil's drink.
truth.causeOfDeath: Cardiac arrest induced by poisoning. The compound acts within 45–90 minutes of ingestion, making the timing consistent with Diane's departure and Veil's deterioration.
truth.coverUp: Diane counted on the CCTV blind spot in the booth section. She knew from a prior visit that the camera covering that area had a recurring overwrite issue — she had mentioned it to the bar manager months ago and he had never fixed it. She wore no distinctive jewelry that night and paid cash.
truth.explanation: Diane poisoned Veil's drink during their argument, using the reach across the table as cover. The vial slipped from her grip in the dark and fell to the cushion. She could not retrieve it without drawing attention. She left believing Veil would be found hours later — long after she was home. She did not account for the napkin falling under the table or for Rask's surveillance photos potentially identifying her.
clueBreakdown: The vial: lab analysis will identify the glycoside compound. Diane's discarded work computer contains browser searches for the same compound class from six months prior.

The cocktail napkin: the partial account numbers match the offshore account linked to Diane. The handwriting is hers — written during the argument as she tried to show Veil she knew what he had found.

Rask's surveillance report: contains photographs of Diane meeting with the fraud bureau's target. She is identifiable in at least two images, which Rask did not know at the time. This places her inside the fraud network Veil was exposing.
The sealed envelope: contains a draft summary of Veil's findings, including account trace documentation. The federal prosecutor will receive it regardless — it was Veil's contingency.
